title: Data Cleansing
text:
The data used was taken from Pro Football Reference’s Stathead service. In order to get all of the player information I wanted, I had to perform multiple queries to pull specific information regarding awards and Super Bowl information. The tables from these queries were then joined together. I handled null values and created standardized “per 16 games” columns to reduce bias towards long careers.



I created a couple of features to be used in a clustering alogrithm for market segmentation. Data came from Dewey Data. I loaded in the parquet files and used PySpark to perform all the engineering. The features are a way to see how long it has been since a customer has come based on their habits as well as how predictable their basket is. All of this with the idea to identify customers that have fallen away from frequency or could easily be interested in sales on certain products.

title: Market Segmentation Feature Engineering
text:
I took convenience store sales data and created a couple of features that would be used by a clustering model to segment a convenience store’s customer base. Ideally this segmentation would be used to identify customers who were perhaps frequent shoppers in the past who have fallen away or high potential customers who could easily made into frequent customers. Data came from Dewey Data. I used PySpark to perform all the engineering.

# Import necessary libraries
import pyspark as spark
import pyspark.sql.functions as sf
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

# Start Spark session
spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()

# Load in necessary tables
shoppers0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_0.parquet")
shoppers1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_1.parquet")
shoppers2 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_2.parquet")
stores = spark.read.parquet("../Data/cstore_stores.parquet")
sets0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/sets_0.parquet")
sets1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/sets_1.parquet")
transactions0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00000.parquet")
transactions1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00001.parquet")
transactions2 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00002.parquet")
transactions3 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00003.parquet")
transactions4 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00004.parquet")
transactions5 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00005.parquet")
transactions6 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00006.parquet")
items = spark.read.parquet("../Data/cstore_master_ctin.parquet")

# Create baseline tables

# Merge items tables
transactions = (
    transactions0
    .unionByName(transactions1)
    .unionByName(transactions2)
    .unionByName(transactions3)
    .unionByName(transactions4)
    .unionByName(transactions5)
    .unionByName(transactions6)
)

# Merge sets tables
sets = sets0.unionByName(sets1)

# Merge shoppers tables
shoppers = (
    shoppers0
    .unionByName(shoppers1)
    .unionByName(shoppers2)
)

# Change data type of Store ID in stores table
stores = stores.withColumn(
    "STORE_ID",
    sf.col("STORE_ID").cast("string")
)

# Create baseline tables

# Join shoppers, transactions, items, and stores tables
joined_items = (shoppers
                .join(transactions, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
                .join(stores, "STORE_ID", how = "left")
                .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
                .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
                .join(items, "GTIN", how = "left"))

# Join shoppers, sets, and stores table. Create columns for year, month, and hour of each transaction set
joined_sets = (shoppers
               .join(sets, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
               .join(stores, on = "STORE_ID", how = "left")
               .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("TIME", sf.hour("DATE_TIME")))

The first feature is the number of cycles it has been since the customer last shop. A cycle is the average number of days between visits. Now customers who have gone longer than normal without shopping at the store can easily be indentified and grouped bny the clustering alogrithm.

# Calculate the number of cycles that have passed since the last time each shopper generated a set using shoppers.SHOPPER_ID, shoppers.TRANSACTION_SET_ID, and sets.DATE_TIME

# Create window for calculations
window = Window.partitionBy("SHOPPER_ID").orderBy(sf.asc("DATE_TIME"))

# Calculate the average days between sets for each shopper, the days between now and their last set, and the divide the days since last set by the average time between sets
final = (joined_sets
    .select("SHOPPER_ID", "DATE_TIME")
    .withColumn("PREVIOUS_SET_DATE_TIME", sf.lag("DATE_TIME").over(window))
    .withColumn("DAYS_BETWEEN_PREVIOUS_PURCHASE", sf.date_diff("DATE_TIME", "PREVIOUS_SET_DATE_TIME"))
    .withColumn("LAST_PURCHASE_DATE", sf.max("DATE_TIME").over(window))
    .withColumn("DAYS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE", sf.date_diff(sf.now(), "LAST_PURCHASE_DATE"))
    .groupBy("SHOPPER_ID")
    .agg(sf.avg("DAYS_BETWEEN_PREVIOUS_PURCHASE").alias("AVERAGE_DAYS_BETWEEN_PURCHASES"), sf.avg("DAYS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE").alias("DAYS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE"))
    .withColumn("ROTATIONS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE", sf.when((sf.col("AVERAGE_DAYS_BETWEEN_PURCHASES").isNotNull()) & (sf.col("AVERAGE_DAYS_BETWEEN_PURCHASES") != 0),  sf.col("DAYS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE")/sf.col("AVERAGE_DAYS_BETWEEN_PURCHASES")).otherwise(None))
    .select("SHOPPER_ID", "ROTATIONS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE"))

display(final.limit(5))

DataFrame[SHOPPER_ID: string, ROTATIONS_SINCE_LAST_PURCHASE: double]


The second feature I created was a sort of basket diversity score. The company might offer discounts on certain items to customers who have a consistent shopping pattern. The score represents the average of the percentage of baskets that every item a customer has purchased appears in. If a customer only buys gas, then gas is in 100% of their baskets, therefore they have a score of 100. If a customer buys cigarettes every time and peanuts half the time, their score is 75% (100% and 50%).

# Calculate The average percent of Total transaction sets every item a shopper has bought appears in for each shopper at every store all time using shoppers.SHOPPER_ID, shoppers.TRANSACTION_SET_ID, and items.GTIN

# Filter joined_items to distinct shopper_id, transaction_set_id, and gtin combinations (we had some problems with duplicate rows instead of quantity being more than 1)
unique_joined_items = joined_items.select("SHOPPER_ID", "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", "GTIN").distinct()

# Calculate the total number of sets by each shopper and filter out those with fewer than 2 sets
total_sets = (joined_sets
              .groupBy("SHOPPER_ID").agg(sf.count("TRANSACTION_SET_ID").alias("TOTAL_SETS"))
              .filter("TOTAL_SETS > 1"))

# Calculate the number of baskets in which an item purchased by a shopper appears
item_appearances = unique_joined_items.groupBy("SHOPPER_ID", "GTIN").agg(sf.countDistinct("TRANSACTION_SET_ID").alias("ITEM_APPEARANCES"))

# Join the total number of sets by each shopper with the number of baskets in which an item purchased by a shopper appears
appearance_percentage = (item_appearances
                         .join(total_sets, on = "SHOPPER_ID", how = "left")
                         .withColumn("APPEARANCE_PERCENTAGE", sf.col("ITEM_APPEARANCES")/sf.col("TOTAL_SETS") * 100)
                         .groupBy("SHOPPER_ID").
                         agg(sf.avg("APPEARANCE_PERCENTAGE").alias("AVERAGE_APPEARANCE_PERCENTAGE")))

display(appearance_percentage.limit(5))

DataFrame[SHOPPER_ID: string, AVERAGE_APPEARANCE_PERCENTAGE: double]

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html()
import sklearn

from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier 
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from xgboost import XGBClassifier
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
import great_tables as gt

general = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbgeneral.csv")

super_bowls = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbsuperbowls.csv")

hof = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbhof.csv")

pro_bowls = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbprobowls.csv")

all_pros = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qballpros.csv")

# 1). Preprocessing data

# Drop rank and player columns from data frames
unwanted_columns = ['Rk', 'Player']
super_bowls = super_bowls.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
hof = hof.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
pro_bowls = pro_bowls.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
all_pros = all_pros.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)

# Get Super Bowl count
super_bowl_count = super_bowls['player_id'].value_counts().reset_index()
super_bowl_count.columns = ['player_id', 'super_bowls']

# Fill hof column with positive
hof['hof'] = 1

# Merge data frames into one
data_frames = [all_pros, super_bowl_count, hof]
df = pd.merge(
    left = general,
    right = pro_bowls,
    how = "left",
    on = "player_id")

for data_frame in data_frames:
    df = pd.merge(
    left = df,
    right = data_frame,
    how = "left",
    on = "player_id")

#Fill N/As
int_columns = ['hof', 'super_bowls', 'Sk', 'Yds.1', 'W', 'L', 'T', '1D']
float_columns = ['Cmp%', 'TD%', 'Int%', 'Rate', 'Sk%', 'Y/A', 'AY/A', 'ANY/A', 'Y/C', 'Succ%', 'Y/A.1', 'Succ%.1']

for column in int_columns:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(0).astype(int)

for column in float_columns:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(0)

# Create Hall of Fame Eligible Column
df['eligible'] = np.where(df['To'] >= 2020, 0, 1)

# Create 16 games column
df['16_games'] = round(df['G'] / 16, 2)

# Create W% column
df['W%'] = round(df['W'] / (df['W'] + df['L'] + df['T']), 2).fillna(0)


# Create per season columns 
df['passing_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['passing_attempts_per_16_games'] = round(df['Att'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['passing_tds_per_16_games'] = round(df['TD'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['int_per_16_games'] = round(df['Int'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['pick_6_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['sacks_per_16_games'] = round(df['Sk'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['sacks_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds.1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['wins_per_16_games'] = round(df['W'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['losses_per_16_games'] = round(df['L'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['ties_per_16_games'] = round(df['T'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games'] = round(df['4QC'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['game_winning_drives_per_16_games'] = round(df['GWD'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds.2'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_tds_per_16_games'] = round(df['TD.1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_first_downs_per_16_games'] = round(df['Sk'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['pro_bowls_per_16_games'] = round(df['Pro_Bowls'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['first_team_all_pros_per_16_games'] = round(df['AP1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['super_bowls_per_16_games'] = round(df['super_bowls'] / df['16_games'], 2)

# Drop more unwanted columns
df = df.drop(columns = ['Rk', 'Age', 'player_id'])

# Rename columns
df.columns = ['player', 'career_start', 'career_end', 'games', 'games_started', 'completions', 'passing_attempts', 'incompletions', 'completion_%', 'passing_yards', 'passing_tds', 'interceptions', 'pick_6s', 'touchdown_%', 'int_%', 'passer_rating', 'sacks_taken', 'sack_yards', 'sack_%', 'passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_net_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'passing_yards_per_completion', 'passing_yards_per_game', 'pass_success_rate', 'wins', 'losses', 'ties', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks', 'game_winning_drives', 'rushing_attempts', 'rushing_yards', 'rushing_yards_per_attempt', 'rushing_touchdowns', 'rushing_yards_per_game', 'rushing_first_downs', 'rush_success_rate', 'pro_bowls', 'first_team_all_pros', 'super_bowls', 'hall_of_fame', 'hall_of_fame_eligible', '16_games', 'winning_%', 'passing_yards_per_16_games', 'passing_attempts_per_16_games', 'passing_tds_per_16_games', 'int_per_16_games', 'pick_6_per_16_games', 'sacks_per_16_games', 'sacks_yards_per_16_games', 'wins_per_16_games', 'losses_per_16_games', 'ties_per_16_games', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games', 'game_winning_drives_per_16_games', 'rushing_yards_per_16_games', 'rushing_tds_per_16_games', 'rushing_first_downs_per_16_games', 'pro_bowls_per_16_games', 'first_team_all_pros_per_16_games', 'super_bowls_per_16_games']

# Scale values using MinMaxScaler
scaler = MinMaxScaler()
numeric_columns = ['games', 'games_started', 'completions', 'passing_attempts', 'incompletions', 'completion_%', 'passing_yards', 'passing_tds', 'interceptions', 'pick_6s', 'touchdown_%', 'int_%', 'passer_rating', 'sacks_taken', 'sack_yards', 'sack_%', 'passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_net_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'passing_yards_per_completion', 'passing_yards_per_game', 'pass_success_rate', 'wins', 'losses', 'ties', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks', 'game_winning_drives', 'rushing_attempts', 'rushing_yards', 'rushing_yards_per_attempt', 'rushing_touchdowns', 'rushing_yards_per_game', 'rushing_first_downs', 'rush_success_rate', 'pro_bowls', 'first_team_all_pros', 'super_bowls', 'hall_of_fame', 'hall_of_fame_eligible', '16_games', 'winning_%', 'passing_yards_per_16_games', 'passing_attempts_per_16_games', 'passing_tds_per_16_games', 'int_per_16_games', 'pick_6_per_16_games', 'sacks_per_16_games', 'sacks_yards_per_16_games', 'wins_per_16_games', 'losses_per_16_games', 'ties_per_16_games', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games', 'game_winning_drives_per_16_games', 'rushing_yards_per_16_games', 'rushing_tds_per_16_games', 'rushing_first_downs_per_16_games', 'pro_bowls_per_16_games', 'first_team_all_pros_per_16_games', 'super_bowls_per_16_games']

for column in numeric_columns:
    df[column] = scaler.fit_transform(df[[column]])

# Split into eligible and ineligible data frames
eligible = df[df['hall_of_fame_eligible'] == 1]
ineligible = df[df['hall_of_fame_eligible'] == 0]

# 2). Selection, training, and use of a machine learning model

# Create X and y from eligible data set
X = eligible.drop(columns = ['hall_of_fame', 'player', 'hall_of_fame_eligible'])
y = eligible['hall_of_fame']

# Split into test and training data
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size = .1, random_state = 12)

# Train model
xg = XGBClassifier(scale_pos_weight = 27.37,
random_state = 12)
xg.fit(X_train, y_train)
xg_prediction = xg.predict(X_test)

# Use XGBoost model to make predictions on ineligible players
Z = ineligible.drop(columns = ['player', 'hall_of_fame_eligible', 'hall_of_fame'])

hof_predictions = xg.predict(Z)

players = pd.DataFrame({
    'player': ineligible['player'].values,
    'Hall of Fame': hof_predictions
}).replace({1:"Yes", 0:"No"}).head(15)

wrong_predict = xg.predict(X)

wrong = pd.DataFrame({
    'player' : eligible['player'].values,
    'real' : eligible['hall_of_fame'].values,
    'predicted' : wrong_predict
}).query('real != predicted').replace({1:"Yes", 0:"No"})



        
        
        



Introduction
The general consensus around the NFL today is that the 1983 draft had the greatest quarterback class of all time. John Elway, Dan Marino, and Jim Kelly combined for 23 Pro Bowls, 11 All Pros, 2 MVPs, 10 Super Bowl Appearances, and 2 Super Bowl Championships. Each made the Hall of Fame.
The consensus runner-up is the 2004 draft class, featuring Eli Manning, Ben Roethlisberger, and Philip Rivers. Given their recent retirements (or coming out of retirement), only Eli Manning is eligible for induction. He has been on the past two ballots but hasn’t been inducted. Roethlisberger will be eligible in 2027 while Rivers reset his 5 year waiting period by coming out of retirement last season.



Stathead QB Comparison


Each player has an interesting case. Phillip Rivers has had no playoff success while Eli Manning won 2 Super Bowl MVPs. Ben Roethlisberger’s resume is a mesh of the two. He doesn’t quite have Rivers’ raw statistics and accolades nor Manning’s playoff impact.
Will the 2004 draft class also have three Hall of Fame inductees? What achievement matters the most? I created a machine learning mdoel to answer those questions.


The Model
I trained an XGBoost classification model using statistics from Pro Football Reference for 90% of the quarterbacks eligible for the Hall of Fame whose stats they have. Stats were taken during the 2025 offseason. (Click the dropdown to see which stats were used)

The other 10% were used to test the model.
Below you’ll see the classification report for the model, but what exactly does it mean?
The main thing to focus on is the top portion. Precision communicates how often the model is right when making the given prediction (separated by the rows). In this case, with either a positive or negative prediction, the model was always right. Recall tells you how many of that kind the model correctly identifies. Once again, the model correctly identified all Hall of Famers and non-Hall of Famers. The f1-score is the harmonic mean of the previous values. It tries to balance precision and recall to give a slightly different accuracy metric. Since the model predicted everything correctly, that difference is lost.

Conclusion
Now to answer the first question. What makes a Hall of Fame career?
Below you’ll find what’s called a feature importance chart. When the model is trying to make its prediction, these are the statistics it has found to be the best predictors of Hall of Fame induction.


Show the code
# Create feature importance plot
important_stats = pd.DataFrame({'importance': xg.feature_importances_,'stat': X_train.columns}).sort_values('importance', ascending = False).query('importance >= .04')

important_stats["importance"] = important_stats["importance"].round(2)

(
    ggplot(
        data = important_stats,
        mapping = aes(
            y = 'importance',
            x = 'stat'))
        + geom_bar(stat = 'identity')
        + geom_text(
          mapping = aes(label = "importance"),
          va = "top",
          nudge_y = .05,
          size = 5 
        )
        + labs(
            x = 'Stat',
            y = 'Importance',
            title = 'What makes a Hall of Famer?',
            subtitle = 'The stats that most strongly predict a Hall of Fame career')
        + theme(
            axis_text_x = element_text(
                hjust=1,
                angle = 45),
            panel_grid = element_blank(),
            axis_line_y = element_blank(),
            axis_ticks_y = element_blank(),
            axis_text_y = element_blank())
)


   
   


When Hall of Fame resumes are discussed, is the pro bowl usually the first thing mentioned? No. The usual suspect, championships, doesn’t weigh heavy at all in the mind of the model. All-Pros and MVPs don’t even have as much weight despite being more prestigious.
Career End adds some context. There are a number of quarterbacks who played over half a century ago that played in the Pro Bowl in almost every season they played in. The model seems to have found a way to filter them out of Hall of Fame inductions by changing the standard based on era (something some sports fans nowadays struggle to do).
Despite its apparent importance in predicting a Hall of Fame career, its importance to the players seems to be declining. One of the headlines before the end of the season was Shedeur Sanders’ invitation the the Pro Bowl. Texans QB CJ Stroud and the Jets’ Justin Fields each declined their invitation to the NFL’s All-Star game. It will be fascinating to see if this trend continnues and if this model will need to be retrained as Pro Bowl selections mean less.
Now it’s time to see whether the model predicts that the 2004 draft class will have 3 Hall of Famers.

title: NFL Hall of Fame Predictor
text:
For this assignment I got my data from Stathead. Thinking primarily about the quarterbacks drafted in 2004, I wanted to see what a predictive model would say about their chanches of being Hall of Famers given their distinct resumes.
Below you will find the process I took to merge multiple data frames, handle null values, and create standardized columns to reduce bias towards players with long career.

# Import necessary libraries and data
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html()
import sklearn
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier 
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from xgboost import XGBClassifier
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE

general = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbgeneral.csv")

super_bowls = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbsuperbowls.csv")

hof = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbhof.csv")

pro_bowls = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qbprobowls.csv")

all_pros = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethanabbott10/Sports_Data/refs/heads/main/data/qballpros.csv")


        
        
        



# 1). Preprocessing data

# Drop unecessary rank and player columns from data frames
unwanted_columns = ['Rk', 'Player']
super_bowls = super_bowls.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
hof = hof.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
pro_bowls = pro_bowls.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)
all_pros = all_pros.drop(columns = unwanted_columns)

# Get Super Bowl count
super_bowl_count = super_bowls['player_id'].value_counts().reset_index()
super_bowl_count.columns = ['player_id', 'super_bowls']

# Fill hof column with positive
hof['hof'] = 1

# Merge data frames into one
data_frames = [all_pros, super_bowl_count, hof]
df = pd.merge(
    left = general,
    right = pro_bowls,
    how = "left",
    on = "player_id")

for data_frame in data_frames:
    df = pd.merge(
    left = df,
    right = data_frame,
    how = "left",
    on = "player_id")

#Fill N/As (all numeric nulls can be 0)
int_columns = ['hof', 'super_bowls', 'Sk', 'Yds.1', 'W', 'L', 'T', '1D']
float_columns = ['Cmp%', 'TD%', 'Int%', 'Rate', 'Sk%', 'Y/A', 'AY/A', 'ANY/A', 'Y/C', 'Succ%', 'Y/A.1', 'Succ%.1']

for column in int_columns:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(0).astype(int)

for column in float_columns:
    df[column] = df[column].fillna(0)

# Create Hall of Fame Eligible Column
df['eligible'] = np.where(df['To'] >= 2020, 0, 1)

# Create 16 games column
df['16_games'] = round(df['G'] / 16, 2)

# Create W% column
df['W%'] = round(df['W'] / (df['W'] + df['L'] + df['T']), 2).fillna(0)


# Create per season columns (I left the other columns but I wanted to ensure that quality players with shorter careers still had a chance without punishing longevity)

df['passing_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['passing_attempts_per_16_games'] = round(df['Att'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['passing_tds_per_16_games'] = round(df['TD'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['int_per_16_games'] = round(df['Int'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['pick_6_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['sacks_per_16_games'] = round(df['Sk'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['sacks_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds.1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['wins_per_16_games'] = round(df['W'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['losses_per_16_games'] = round(df['L'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['ties_per_16_games'] = round(df['T'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games'] = round(df['4QC'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['game_winning_drives_per_16_games'] = round(df['GWD'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_yards_per_16_games'] = round(df['Yds.2'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_tds_per_16_games'] = round(df['TD.1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['rushing_first_downs_per_16_games'] = round(df['Sk'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['pro_bowls_per_16_games'] = round(df['Pro_Bowls'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['first_team_all_pros_per_16_games'] = round(df['AP1'] / df['16_games'], 2)
df['super_bowls_per_16_games'] = round(df['super_bowls'] / df['16_games'], 2)

# Drop more unwanted columns
df = df.drop(columns = ['Rk', 'Age', 'player_id'])

# Rename columns
df.columns = ['player', 'career_start', 'career_end', 'games', 'games_started', 'completions', 'passing_attempts', 'incompletions', 'completion_%', 'passing_yards', 'passing_tds', 'interceptions', 'pick_6s', 'touchdown_%', 'int_%', 'passer_rating', 'sacks_taken', 'sack_yards', 'sack_%', 'passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_net_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'passing_yards_per_completion', 'passing_yards_per_game', 'pass_success_rate', 'wins', 'losses', 'ties', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks', 'game_winning_drives', 'rushing_attempts', 'rushing_yards', 'rushing_yards_per_attempt', 'rushing_touchdowns', 'rushing_yards_per_game', 'rushing_first_downs', 'rush_success_rate', 'pro_bowls', 'first_team_all_pros', 'super_bowls', 'hall_of_fame', 'hall_of_fame_eligible', '16_games', 'winning_%', 'passing_yards_per_16_games', 'passing_attempts_per_16_games', 'passing_tds_per_16_games', 'int_per_16_games', 'pick_6_per_16_games', 'sacks_per_16_games', 'sacks_yards_per_16_games', 'wins_per_16_games', 'losses_per_16_games', 'ties_per_16_games', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games', 'game_winning_drives_per_16_games', 'rushing_yards_per_16_games', 'rushing_tds_per_16_games', 'rushing_first_downs_per_16_games', 'pro_bowls_per_16_games', 'first_team_all_pros_per_16_games', 'super_bowls_per_16_games']

# Scale values using MinMaxScaler (Bound all numbers between 0 and 1 to weaken the bias towards columns such as passing yards which contain large values, model will be able to better understand the difference between players at each position in the context of all columns)

scaler = MinMaxScaler()
numeric_columns = ['games', 'games_started', 'completions', 'passing_attempts', 'incompletions', 'completion_%', 'passing_yards', 'passing_tds', 'interceptions', 'pick_6s', 'touchdown_%', 'int_%', 'passer_rating', 'sacks_taken', 'sack_yards', 'sack_%', 'passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'adjusted_net_passing_yards_per_attempt', 'passing_yards_per_completion', 'passing_yards_per_game', 'pass_success_rate', 'wins', 'losses', 'ties', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks', 'game_winning_drives', 'rushing_attempts', 'rushing_yards', 'rushing_yards_per_attempt', 'rushing_touchdowns', 'rushing_yards_per_game', 'rushing_first_downs', 'rush_success_rate', 'pro_bowls', 'first_team_all_pros', 'super_bowls', 'hall_of_fame', 'hall_of_fame_eligible', '16_games', 'winning_%', 'passing_yards_per_16_games', 'passing_attempts_per_16_games', 'passing_tds_per_16_games', 'int_per_16_games', 'pick_6_per_16_games', 'sacks_per_16_games', 'sacks_yards_per_16_games', 'wins_per_16_games', 'losses_per_16_games', 'ties_per_16_games', 'fourth_quarter_comebacks_per_16_games', 'game_winning_drives_per_16_games', 'rushing_yards_per_16_games', 'rushing_tds_per_16_games', 'rushing_first_downs_per_16_games', 'pro_bowls_per_16_games', 'first_team_all_pros_per_16_games', 'super_bowls_per_16_games']

for column in numeric_columns:
    df[column] = scaler.fit_transform(df[[column]])

# Split into eligible and ineligible data frames (I'll split the eligible players to train and then use the model to predict on uneligible players)
eligible = df[df['hall_of_fame_eligible'] == 1]
ineligible = df[df['hall_of_fame_eligible'] == 0]
